judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Vacant' is defined by a 31%-of-square-footage test tied to 'customary operations' — a defined but still fact-laden term, and the tenant/owner split is clearly drawn. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with the Vacancy Provisions in b. and with 'Rental Value'/'tenantability' in the Business Income form; a partially rented apartment complex could create friction but nothing contradictory. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 60-day trigger, a closed list of six barred perils and a flat 15% reduction; all quantified. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits against the 'suspension'/'untenantability' concepts in the Business Income form but does not contradict them. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Valuation defaults to 'actual cash value', a term not defined in this form, and again carves out ordinance-driven cost. The ACV baseline is a classic construction battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 B. adds a definition of 'Actual Cash Value', while the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage (shown in the Declarations) replaces ACV entirely — so three provisions govern the same measure. Real but manageable interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Applicability sentence only. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Accurately describes the layering. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The condition turns on 'the value of Covered Property at the time of loss' measured against 'the Limit of Insurance for the property', and the printed step (2) is cut off mid-sentence — leaving the four-step penalty formula incomplete on the page. Both the valuation input and the truncation give a court something to work with.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applied to a 100% blanket limit covering nine buildings it must be read with b. (one limit applying to two or more items), with the Declarations' blanket summary, and with the blanket-limit sub-cap in the Increased Cost Of Construction coverage. Those interactions are genuinely contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: In this printing the Mortgageholders condition is interleaved with fragments of Agreed Value and Inflation Guard, so the text as presented runs together two different conditions and breaks off. That garbling obscures meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 C.4 replaces paragraph b. for townhouse risks only, and no mortgageholder is shown in the Declarations. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence excluding 'the increased cost attributable to enforcement of any ordinance or law regulating the construction, use or repair of any property' — 'attributable to' and the reach of 'any ordinance or law' are exactly the words a code-upgrade dispute turns on. Short, absolute and contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It flatly excludes what the Increased Cost Of Construction Additional Coverage (A.4.e) grants, and A.4.e.(9) expressly says the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage does not include that cost while the ICC amount 'is not subject to such limitation'. The same carve-out is repeated in Loss Payment E.4.b and Valuation E.7.b, and the Ordinance Or Law Exclusion B.1.a compounds it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional extension keyed to a Declarations election, with a clear contract-based valuation cap. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage being shown; the Declarations do show Replacement Cost but not this extension. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed definition of 'Fungus'. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the identical definition in CP 10 30 G.1 and the CGL 'Fungi' definition. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant or contaminant, including smoke, vapor, soot, fumes, acids, alkalis, chemicals and waste' is the famously over-broad pollution definition — a general phrase followed by illustrative specifics. Genuinely argued in many cases, though not obviously in issue here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated verbatim in CP 00 30 F.4 and CGL V.15, so the instrument is internally consistent. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed definition of 'Stock'. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Covered Property and the Causes of Loss form. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Second printing of the first-named-insured cancellation right; identical substance and plain. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c005 without variance. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clean 10/30-day cancellation mechanics. Nothing to name.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line notice-address rule. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c007 and matches IL 02 61 B.2. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clean audit right with a fixed three-year tail. Nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short anti-stacking rule; definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific time and place; definite. Nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reading instruction only. Nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations do show 'SPECIAL FORM' for each blanket coverage, so the condition is satisfied. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The anti-concurrent-causation lead-in ('regardless of any other cause or event that contributes concurrently or in any sequence') is one of the most litigated formulations in property insurance. Its reach is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with the many 'but if ... results in fire, we will pay' exceptions in the same section and with the ensuing-loss structure of B.2 and B.3. Some tension, though the form is built to accommodate it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The enforcement of any ordinance or law ... Regulating the construction, use or repair of any property' is absolute and sweeping, and it applies whether or not the loss caused the enforcement. In a fire claim on a code-regulated apartment building this is the kind of language parties fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Increased Cost Of Construction Additional Coverage says in terms that it 'is not subject to the terms of the Ordinance or Law Exclusion, to the extent that such Exclusion would conflict' — the policy itself anticipates the conflict. It also bears on the Period of Restoration's ordinance carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Earth movement enumerated in five sub-items with a fire/explosion ensuing-loss exception; detailed and closed. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the anti-concurrent lead-in and the specified-causes definition. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Seizure or destruction by governmental order, with an express firefighting exception. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with the Civil Authority Additional Coverage in the Business Income form. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Nuclear Energy Liability endorsement, which addresses liability coverages only. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Failure includes lack of sufficient capacity and reduction in supply' is defined; the off-premises trigger is clear. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly hands off to Special Exclusion B.4.a.(1) for Business Income and Extra Expense, which is present. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: War exclusion in three enumerated limbs; standard and definite. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly defers to the Limited Coverage For Fungus in section E, which is present with its own $15,000 cap. Coherent.
